title: S&P DJI December quarterly rebalance takes effect at the open — S&P 500/100/400/600 membership, share and float changes implemented at the 2027-12-17 close
source: EST: THE INDEX OWNER'S OWN EFFECTIVE-DATE WORDING, APPLIED FORWARD -- not a fetched 2027 S&P DJI schedule. This repo already holds that wording verbatim: sp-quarterly-rebalance-effective-2026-09-21 re-extracted press.spglobal.com's 2026-09-04 release, whose effective-date sentence reads 'effective prior to the open of trading on Monday, September 21, 2026, to coincide with the quarterly rebalance' -- the Monday following that quarter's third Friday (2026-09-18), with the changes implemented at that Friday's close. Applied to December 2027: the third Friday is 2027-12-17 (confirmed on OCC's own 2027 calendar by this proposal's own event, opex-2027-12-17), so the rebalance is effective prior to the open on MONDAY 2027-12-20 and implemented at the 2027-12-17 close. Corroborated by the calendar's own sibling row sp-rebalance-reference-close-2027-03-12, which places the March 2027 reference close on the second Friday, one week ahead of that quarter's third Friday -- the same relative geometry. THE METHODOLOGY PRIMARY WAS ATTEMPTED AND BLOCKED: spglobal.com/spdji/en/documents/methodologies/methodology-sp-us-indices.pdf returned HTTP 403 this session (2026-09-08, recorded in the proposer's ledger probe-ref.blocked), so no rebalancing-schedule clause was read directly and nothing was silently substituted. Filed estimate on three counts: the forward application of a rule read from one instance rather than from the methodology itself; the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts having no member for an index owner's own published schedule, the same gap sp-quarterly-rebalance-effective-2026-09-21 and every Russell entry record; and this lane's no-self-confirm limit on an event discovered in-sweep. Discovered during the opex-2027-12-17 initial research, checked 2026-09-08
notes: PROPOSED by the opex-2027-12-17 initial research (2026-09-08) as a dated event inside the proposer's +/-5-day corridor (D+3) that this calendar holds for no 2027 quarter. THIS IS THE MECHANISM ONE OF THE PROPOSER'S OWN PROPOSALS FLAGGED AND DID NOT RESEARCH: proposals/opex-2027-12-17.from-consumer-confidence-2027-12-22.json warned that 'December triple witching is the one expiration that also carries annual index reconstitution flow in some index families; this lane did not research that and makes no claim about it'. Filing this entry is how that flag gets discharged -- the December S&P quarterly rebalance is implemented at the third Friday's close, i.e. at the proposer's own settlement, which is a real structural adjacency and the only December-specific mechanism the proposer could name. THE PROPOSER THEN REFUSES THE OBVIOUS INFERENCE, ON ITS OWN MEASUREMENTS. The rebalance recurs EVERY quarter, so it cannot explain anything December-specific, and the proposer measured December quarterly expirations indistinguishable from the other three quarterly months on all three channels (VIX -0.715 vs -0.201 P = 0.198; |S&P| 0.774% vs 0.688% P = 0.693; following-five-session realized vol 0.793 vs 0.988 P = 0.372; no cell in the twelve-cell Mar/Jun/Sep/Dec family under 0.05). The precedent for this proposal is exact and its own follow-through is the caution: opex-2026-09-18's adjacency sweep proposed sp-quarterly-rebalance-effective-2026-09-21 the same way, and that event's initial research found the September 2026 'deletions' were tier MIGRATIONS inside the S&P Composite 1500 rather than expulsions -- ten of the release's moves -- which materially changed what the closing imbalance meant. A taking lane should expect the same and re-extract the December 2027 release rather than inherit a headline. WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED HERE: the annual NASDAQ-100 reconstitution, which is a different index family on a different announcement path and which this lane did not research; and any membership names, which will not exist until S&P DJI publishes the December 2027 release. This entry is a date and a corridor position. Proposed as an estimate; nothing here licenses an entry.
